description:
F14: spec's 'two snapshot reads + one diff + one ETS insert' hot-path claim understates O(modules × lines) reads twice per test + ExUnit OnExitHandler deep-copies; fix boundary_hook_sync spec text + Boundary moduledoc + docs cost tables, then chain windows (tail(N) = head(N+1)) so the closure captures only {module, name}. F12: per_test_requirement_reach/3 recomputed once per subject — call once per review with full closure_map. F26: a formatter crash leaves the previous run's artifact on disk with task exit 0 — assert artifact freshness (generated_at vs pre-suite timestamp) and Mix.raise on miss. Report F14/F12/F26.

---

## Orchestrator scoping (synthesized 2026-07-25 by /orchestrate-epic from verified code analysis)

## specled_-dn4.6 — Correct the per-test cost model + artifact freshness guard (F14, F12, F26)

**Advances:** `specled.coverage_capture`, `specled.spec_review`

Matched obligations:

- `specled.coverage_capture.boundary_hook_sync` (`.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:448-459`) — the false claim is verbatim at :456-457: *"The hot path is two snapshot reads + one `Snapshot.diff/2` + one ETS insert; no `module_info/1` calls; the head snapshot lives only in the `on_exit` closure."* Scenario `scenario.boundary_hook_window` (:785-794).
- `specled.coverage_capture.per_test_v2_envelope` (:284-303) — the artifact-write contract F26's freshness guard enforces; `specled.coverage_capture.serialized_run` (:144-152) is the task-side requirement.
- `specled.spec_review.coverage_tab_v2_envelope_data_layer` (`.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md:383-413`) — F12's hoist changes how `build_v2/2` computes reach; `specled.spec_review.coverage_generated_at_staleness` (:356-362) is the neighboring `generated_at` obligation F26's guard leans on.

**Primary files:**

*F14 — cost model.*

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/boundary.ex:2-13` moduledoc, verbatim *"Hot path is two snapshot reads + one `Snapshot.diff/2` + one ETS insert — no `module_info/1` calls, and the head snapshot lives only in the `on_exit` closure (never retained outside it)."* Each "snapshot read" is `config.snapshot_fn.(modules)` (:46, :70) which is `Snapshot.take/2` over the whole module scope — O(modules × lines), twice per test.
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:456-457` — same claim in the requirement.
- `docs/coverage.md:171-177` — the **Cost model** paragraph ("two suite-level snapshots from the formatter and two snapshots per hooked test from the boundary hook"). This is where the ticket's *"publish one measured per-test overhead figure"* sibling item (dn4.9) also lands.
- the chained-window change: `lib/specled_ex/coverage.ex:52-67` `per_test_boundary/1` — today the `on_exit` closure at :61-63 captures `head_snapshot` (an entire module snapshot) by value, which `ExUnit.OnExitHandler` then deep-copies. `tail(N) = head(N+1)` means the closure captures only `{module, name}`, i.e. `key`. Touches `Boundary.head/1` (:38-48) and `Boundary.tail` (:54-84) too.

*F12 — recomputation per subject.* Verified: `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:358-380` is `Map.new(subject_reqs, fn {subject_id, {subject, requirements}} -> …)`, and inside it `v2_by_requirement/6` (:500-548) calls `CoverageTriangulation.per_test_requirement_reach(envelope.payload, closure_map, line_index)` at :511 with a `closure_map` containing exactly **one** subject (built at :359-363). So the full payload is regrouped and re-walked once per subject. Note `line_index` is already correctly memoized for the build (:340-356) — the fix is to give `per_test_requirement_reach/3` the full multi-subject `closure_map` once and index the result, mirroring how the aggregate clause could too (:463-498).

*F26 — artifact freshness.* Verified absent: `lib/mix/tasks/spec.cover.test.ex:180-219` `defp run_per_test/2` ends with `try do Mix.Task.run("test", ["--cover" | argv]) after (async warning) end` — no post-suite assertion that `.spec/_coverage/per_test.coverdata` was rewritten. A formatter crash inside the GenServer leaves the previous run's artifact and the task still exits 0. `Store.read_status/1` and the envelope's `generated_at` are the available signals; `Mix.raise` is the established failure idiom in this file (:135, :150, :170, :184).

**Allowed touches (globs):**

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/boundary.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex`
- `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex` (only if `per_test_requirement_reach/3`'s contract needs the multi-subject shape spelled out)
- `lib/mix/tasks/spec.cover.test.ex`
- `docs/coverage.md`
- `test/specled_ex/coverage/boundary_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/case_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs`
- `test/mix/tasks/spec_cover_test_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md`
- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md`
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.per_test_sync_boundary.md`
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

**Out of Scope (files):** `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex` (dn4.2/4.4/4.5), `lib/specled_ex/coverage/store.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex`, `.spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md`, `.spec/specs/package.spec.md`, `docs/adoption.md`, `docs/concepts.md`.

**Out of Scope (intent):**

- Chaining windows is a **semantic** change to exclusivity, not a perf tweak: `tail(N)` becoming `head(N+1)` means anything running *between* two tests (ExUnit's own `setup_all`, the runner) lands in the next test's window. Either prove that interval is empty or state the new bound in `specled.decision.per_test_sync_boundary.md` — do not ship a silently widened claim under the old "exact up to escaped processes" wording.
- Fix the cost claim to be *true*, not to be flattering. Do not delete the claim (that would be weakening a `must`).
- F26 raises on a **stale** artifact; it must not raise merely because the suite was red — `default_aggregate_red_suite_passthrough` (:182-189) already fixes exit-code semantics for the aggregate lane and the per-test lane must not regress into swallowing or inventing failures.
- No new deps.

**Verification:**

- `mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/boundary_test.exs test/specled_ex/case_test.exs test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs test/mix/tasks/spec_cover_test_test.exs`
- `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`, then `mix spec.check`
- Stubs, all **`execute: true`**: `coverage_capture.spec.md:913-928` (`serialized_run`, `per_test_v2_envelope`, `boundary_hook_sync`, `per_test_exclusive_attribution`), :943-947 (`boundary_noop_unarmed`); `spec_review.spec.md:805-810` (`coverage_tab_v2_envelope_data_layer` via `coverage_closure_test.exs`).
- The docs edit has no executing stub — `docs/coverage.md` is not a `source_file` verification target in any spec today, so the cost-model correction is verified by review only.

**Overlap risk:**

- `lib/specled_ex/coverage/boundary.ex` + `lib/specled_ex/coverage.ex` — **dn4.1** (deletes the `tags` argument from the very `Boundary.tail` call at `coverage.ex:62` that dn4.6 rewrites to drop the `head_snapshot` capture), **dn4.4** (resolver), **dn4.9** (`head/1` tolerance, rescue insert, `boundary_key/1` `setup_all` fallback at `coverage.ex:69-71`). Sequence after dn4.1 and dn4.4.
- `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex` — **dn4.5** (`v2_by_requirement/6`'s `:per_test` clause at :500-548, the same function F12 restructures).
- `docs/coverage.md` — **dn4.9** (both docs items land in the same two paragraphs: :171-177 cost model, :185-217 wiring).
- `.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md` — **dn4.1, dn4.3, dn4.4, dn4.5, dn4.8**.

Cold verification of d60ffa6 on `specled_-dn4.6/cost-model-freshness` (base ca7ef09). Worktree left byte-clean after three mutation probes.

## Mechanical checks

- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — clean
- `mix test` (full suite, not just targeted) — 3 properties, 1215 tests, 0 failures
- `mix test` targeted set + blast radius (`boundary_test`, `case_test`, `coverage_closure_test`, `spec_cover_test_test`, `html_test`, `formatter_test`) — 166 tests, 0 failures
- `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` — status=pass, errors=0, warnings=0
- `mix spec.check` (bare) — status=pass, errors=0, warnings=0
- `mix format --check-formatted` — clean
- `mix deps.unlock --check-unused` — clean
- Known flake zr6 not hit.

Scope: 13 files, all inside Allowed globs. `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex` and `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex` untouched (absent from the diff entirely, not name-only). `realization_hashes.json` moved exactly two keys — `SpecLedEx.Coverage` and `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Boundary.tail/2` — both genuine (`tail/2`'s parameters and guards changed from `(test_key, head_snapshot)` to `(module, name)`). No requirement ids removed.

The single `spec.check` append_only WARNING (`specled.decision.coverage_qualifier_requirement_ids` self-authorization) is dn4.8's, introduced in commit 91987f7 and present at base — not dn4.6's.

## Semantic checks

**F14 chaining mechanics — correct.** `Boundary.head/1` caches the initial whole-scope snapshot in the boundary table under `@head_snapshot_key`; `tail/2` reads it, diffs, and inserts `{{module, name}, row}` plus the new chained head in one `:ets.insert/2`. The `on_exit` closure in `Coverage.per_test_boundary/1` captures only `key`; the new `tail/2` arity makes passing a snapshot structurally impossible, so "the closure retains only the test key" is proven by construction rather than by assertion.

The load-bearing detail nobody flagged: the reserved atom head-snapshot row lands in the same public table the formatter flushes from, and `formatter.ex` was out of scope so it could not be adapted. It is safe — `Arming.boundary_index/1` (arming.ex:42-46) filters rows on `is_tuple(key) and is_map(row)`, and the head row's key is an atom, so it falls through to the drop clause. Verified, not assumed.

**Chaining test is genuine.** Reverting `head/1`'s ETS reuse (probe D) fails "chains each tail into the next head..." with a `FunctionClauseError` from snapshot exhaustion, and additionally fails dn4.4's modules-cache test. `Agent.get(agent, & &1) == []` pins exactly three reads for two tests: fewer leaves a non-empty list, more crashes. It could not pass under the old two-reads-per-test implementation.

**F12 hoist — provably output-identical, and the test proves more than call count.** Both `per_test_requirement_reach/3` (coverage_triangulation.ex:278-295) and `aggregate_requirement_reach/2` (:877-894) are plain folds over `subjects` delegating to per-requirement helpers that take no `subject_id`, derive their indexes solely from the envelope / `line_index`, and never read `info.owned_files`. Widening the closure map from one subject to all cannot change any `{subject_id, req_id}` entry. The new test asserts once-ness (`refute_receive`), the full two-subject map shape, and both subjects' `covered_mfas` — so equal output for a multi-subject fixture is covered, not just the seam.

**F26 tests hit the real task path.** `run_fixture_mix_test/2` (test_support/specled_ex_integration_case.ex:74-87) is a real `System.cmd("mix", args, cd: root)` child BEAM with real exit status — no seam substitution.

**Timestamp hazards — clear.** `generated_at` defaults to `DateTime.utc_now()` (store.ex:141) at microsecond precision with no truncation anywhere, round-trips losslessly through `term_to_binary`, and is compared against a same-BEAM `DateTime.utc_now()`. Same-second and previous-run-same-second collisions are not hazards, and no file mtime is involved. Residual: wall clock, not monotonic, so an NTP step backwards mid-suite would false-positive. Acceptable; noted only.

**The chained-window restatement on the capture side is honest and complete.** Checked against the actual mechanics in coverage.ex + boundary.ex: with `--per-test` forcing a serialized run, the interval between `tail(N)` and test N+1's body contains ExUnit runner bookkeeping, `setup_all`/`setup` callbacks, and any intervening unhooked tests — exactly what the new wording discloses. It is not merely restated in the ADR; it propagated coherently through coverage_capture.spec.md's summary (:32), `serialized_run` (:359), `boundary_row_exclusive` (:524), `per_test_exclusive_attribution` (:541), `remainder`/`unhooked_degrade` (:581-596), and both affected scenarios (:852, :945), plus docs/coverage.md. The cost claim became true rather than deleted. This half of the semantic risk passes.

## Verdict

FAIL — two independent gaps. F14's chaining mechanics and F12's hoist are correct and well covered; the failures are (A) the review surface now over-claims relative to the spec dn4.6 itself edited, and (B) F26's defining clause has no covering test.

## Gaps

**Gap A — the widened claim landed in `spec_review.spec.md` but not on the surface a reviewer reads, and left the spec self-contradictory.**

dn4.6 rewrote `specled.spec_review.coverage_exact_up_to_escaped_processes_qualifier` (spec_review.spec.md:322-336) to claim "exact within the disclosed chained window (later windows include the serialized interval since the prior tail, in addition to escaped-process leakage)", and that requirement demands the closure line, "Reached by tests" row, Self-verified row, and rollup badge "shall each be discoverably qualified with **that** claim". Nothing downstream carries the widened claim:

- `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex` still renders the narrow bound at five sites — `@exact_up_to_escaped_title` (:3101, used at :3133), the visible "(exact up to escaped processes)" strings (:2037, :3074, :3154), and the degraded titles (:2055-2058, :2735, :3071, :3130). The title text asserts the only caveat is a process outliving its tail snapshot. A reviewer is now told a *narrower* bound than the spec admits, which is the over-claim the orchestrator ruling forbids — inverted onto the review lane.
- The two scenarios that **cover** that very requirement still require the old string: `coverage_qualifies_exact_up_to_escaped` (:717-728) demands a discoverable "(exact up to escaped processes)" qualifier on three surfaces, and `coverage_card_rollup_badge_renders` (:750-760) demands a "title caveat citing escaped processes". `html_test.exs:1297,1307,1572,1573` assert those strings. So the requirement statement and its own covering scenarios now contradict each other, and the suite enforces the side dn4.6 retired.
- Two sibling requirements in the same file were left on the narrow wording and now contradict the edited one: `coverage_line_mfa_intersection_qualifier` (:337-346, "shall carry the exact-up-to-escaped-processes qualifier") and `coverage_rollup_badge` (:348-357, "the ... disclaimer (exact-up-to-escaped-processes ...)").
- `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:209` — **in scope for dn4.6** — still documents `:ok_per_test` as "exact up to escaped processes". No scope excuse applies here.

`html.ex` is explicitly Out of Scope, so the correct handling was either to leave spec_review.spec.md's claim wording to the stage that owns the renderer, or to edit it *and* update the affected scenarios *and* record the renderer work as a deferred obligation. `.claude/rules/specled.md` requires step 2 ("Update affected scenarios") on any requirement rewrite; it was skipped, and the IMPLEMENTED comment reports "Deferred must requirements: none". `mix spec.check` cannot catch this — the contradiction is prose-level.

Also still on the retired claim, out of scope but now untracked: `docs/adoption.md:26,387-390`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex:12`, `.spec/specs/package.spec.md:29` (whose summary asserts docs/coverage.md carries the "exact up to escaped processes" claim — docs/coverage.md no longer does).

**Gap B — `per_test_artifact_freshness`'s freshness comparison is untested; the stale test passes via a different clause.**

Proven by mutation. Neutering only the freshness comparison in `assert_fresh_per_test_artifact!` (replacing `:gt <- DateTime.compare(generated_at, suite_started_at)` with a tautology, leaving the status and `read_v2` clauses intact) leaves both new tests green — 12 tests, 0 failures, including `output =~ "coverage artifact is stale"`.

Why: `scaffold_empty_fixture`'s child suite touches no application code, so the formatter refuses, and `Store.write_v2`'s empty-files gate (store.ex:203) rewrites the status sidecar to `{:refused, :empty_files}` while leaving the pre-written 2020 artifact file untouched. The guard therefore raises on `{:ok, _stats} <- Store.read_status(path)`. Removing the guard entirely (probe C) does fail the test, so it is not vacuous — it proves *a* guard exists, just not the freshness one.

The consequence is that the exact failure F26 was written for is uncovered: a formatter that dies *before* reaching `write_v2` leaves a successful `{:ok, stats}` sidecar **and** the previous run's artifact, and only the `generated_at` vs pre-suite comparison catches it. Scenario `specled.coverage_capture.scenario.spec_cover_test_per_test_freshness`'s "instead of accepting the previous run's file" passes for the wrong reason. Requirement text ("`Store.read_v2/1` to return an envelope whose `generated_at` is later than a timestamp captured immediately before the suite started") is the clause with no covering test. A fixture whose formatter is armed, produces hits, and is then made to crash between capture and write — or one that pre-writes a stale-but-successful `{:ok, stats}` sidecar *after* the suite runs is not possible, so the crash-injection seam is the honest route — would close it.

## Notes

- Cost-model honesty, one gap in the disclosure: chaining removes ExUnit's `OnExitHandler` deep copy of the head snapshot but adds an ETS write copy plus an ETS read copy of the whole snapshot per hooked test, and retains the final tail in the table for the rest of the run. The spec and docs say "ETS operations per hooked test", which is not false, but the ADR's Context and Positive bullets say only that chaining "removes that copy" and never mention the two it adds. Since F14 exists specifically to stop understating cost, naming the ETS copies would be consistent with the ticket's intent. Not a gate.
- `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Boundary.head/1` is a tracked realization (realization_hashes.json:211) whose public return contract flipped from `Snapshot.module_snapshot() | :unarmed` to `:armed | :unarmed`, with no hash bump. That is correct behavior for the api_boundary tier — `ApiBoundary.hash/2` hashes `canonicalize_head/1`, and `def head(_context)` is textually unchanged — but it means the drift gate did not see a real public-contract change. Not dn4.6's defect; worth knowing before leaning on hash movement as the whole drift story.
- `boundary_key/1` (coverage.ex:69-71) still has a single `%{module:, test:}` clause, so `per_test_boundary/1` raises in a `setup_all` context. Unchanged by dn4.6 (the key is still computed in setup, only the destructuring moved into the closure); dn4.9 owns the fallback.
- If a hooked test's `on_exit` tail raises, the chained head is not advanced and the next test's window silently absorbs the failed test's coverage. Not disclosed in the new bound. Low severity, but it is a third leakage path alongside the two the ADR now names.
- `case_test.exs`'s added `Agent.get(agent, &length/1) == 1` pins that `head/1` takes exactly one snapshot for a single hooked test. Real but weak — it does not distinguish chained from unchained, since a single test reads one snapshot either way. The chaining proof lives entirely in `boundary_test.exs`.

title: Correct the per-test cost model + artifact freshness guard (F14, F12, F26)
